notes:
You can now move your licence to another Mac yourself.

The terms have always said a licence covers up to three Macs and that you
deactivate one to move it. Until now there was no way to do the deactivating —
you had to write in and ask, which is not what the page you agreed to said.

    docket licence --deactivate

That releases the activation this Mac is holding, so you can activate Docket on
a different one with the same key.

It only ever releases this Mac's own activation. There is deliberately no way
to pass in someone else's — on a licence shared with colleagues, that would be
a way to switch off a machine that is not yours.

Docket confirms the release by asking the payment provider afterwards whether
the activation is really gone, rather than assuming the request worked. If it
cannot reach the provider, nothing is changed at either end and it tells you so,
so a failed attempt can never leave you holding an activation you can no longer
release.

If your Mac is lost, broken, or already wiped, you cannot run this on it — write
to the address on the contact page and the activation will be freed for you.

Nothing in your audits changes in this release.
